name: Tesamorelin (off-label)
route: Injection under the skin; compounded copies are unapproved
status: Approved as Egrifta only for abdominal fat in HIV lipodystrophy; compounded and wellness use is off-label and unapproved
mechanism: Stimulates the pituitary to release growth hormone, which raises IGF-1 and shrinks deep belly fat in people with HIV lipodystrophy
uses: Visceral fat loss (approved only in HIV lipodystrophy)

article.summary: Tesamorelin is FDA-approved as Egrifta only to cut belly fat in adults with HIV lipodystrophy. Clinics also sell off-label or compounded versions for anti-aging and fat loss, without approval or proof.
article.takeaway: Tesamorelin is a lab-made version of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) that makes the pituitary release more growth hormone. The FDA approved it as Egrifta for one use, reducing excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy, where visceral fat fell 15% versus a 5% rise on placebo.[^1][^2] Using it for general weight loss, muscle or anti-aging is off-label, and the label says it is not for weight loss and that long-term cardiovascular safety is not established.[^2] Compounded copies are not FDA-approved products, and WADA bans tesamorelin.[^3]
glance: Approved as Egrifta SV and WR only for excess abdominal fat in HIV lipodystrophy[^2]

Phase 3 trials in HIV; small trials in fatty liver and in older adults' cognition[^4][^5]

blocks.text: The hypothalamus releases GHRH, which tells the pituitary to release growth hormone in pulses. Growth hormone raises IGF-1, and together they reduce visceral fat, the deep belly fat around organs. Tesamorelin is a stabilized GHRH analog, so it works through the body's own pituitary rather than supplying growth hormone directly. In the main trial IGF-1 rose 81%.[^1]

rows: Visceral fat down 15.2% vs up 5.0% on placebo; triglycerides fell[^1]
Fat loss held at 18% while treated, and fat returned after stopping[^6]
61 people with HIV and fatty liver
Liver fat fell 4.1 percentage points more than on placebo[^4]
152 older adults, with or without mild cognitive impairment
Favorable effect on cognition; IGF-1 rose 117%[^5]

blocks.text: Most controlled data are in people with HIV, plus small trials in older adults. Evidence for general fat loss or anti-aging in otherwise healthy people is thin.

items: **Raised IGF-1:** the label says the effects of prolonged IGF-1 elevation are unknown and that IGF-1 should be monitored[^2]
**Tumors:** growth hormone is a growth factor, so active cancer is a reason not to use it[^2]
**Fluid and sugar:** swelling, joint pain, carpal tunnel syndrome, glucose intolerance and diabetes can occur[^2]
**Long term:** long-term cardiovascular safety is not established, and visceral fat returns after stopping[^2][^6]
**Compounded copies:** not reviewed by the FDA for safety, effectiveness or quality; illegally sold peptides have shown low purity and toxic metals[^7]

blocks.text: Egrifta SV and Egrifta WR are FDA-approved for reducing excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy and are not indicated for weight loss.[^2] A clinician can prescribe an approved drug off-label, but a compounded copy is not an approved product. WADA prohibits tesamorelin, as a GHRH analog, at all times.[^3] See [tesamorelin](/peptides/tesamorelin) for the approved drug.

Tesamorelin works for the one thing it is approved for and clearly raises growth hormone and IGF-1. Off-label use for fat loss or anti-aging relies on small studies and on long-term effects that are unknown in healthy people. Athletes subject to testing should treat it as banned.

evidence.label: Mixed: solid for HIV belly fat, thin elsewhere
evidence.text: Randomized phase 3 trials support the approved use.[^1] Other uses rest on small or short trials.[^4][^5]

faq.q: Is compounded tesamorelin the same as Egrifta?
faq.a: Egrifta SV and WR are the FDA-approved tesamorelin products. A compounded 'tesamorelin' is a pharmacy-made copy that the FDA has not reviewed for quality or effectiveness.[^2]

faq.q: Does it work for weight loss?
faq.a: No. The label says Egrifta is not indicated for weight loss because it has a weight-neutral effect; it targets visceral fat in a specific population.[^2]
No. WADA prohibits GHRH analogs, including tesamorelin, at all times.[^3]
